Synopsis:
Locke and Marrick are parents who are scared for their daughter Arabella. Taken by the druids, Arabella is appearing in court on accusations of thievery. Her parents have no doubt that she is guilty but they are terrified for her and trying to get to her.Marrick hides his concern throughout with anger and threats of violence. It is easier to deal with fury then it is to temper fear. Locke is more level-headed but no less close to violence. Marrick and Locke are both at the entrance to the inner grove and the sacred pool and have just been denied entry.

Cluster Contexts:
- DEN_GuardedEntrance_Parents.json: Locke and Marrick are standing at the entrance to the inner grove and sacred pool, just denied entry while desperate to reach their daughter Arabella, who was taken by the druids and is now being held in a court on accusations of stealing a druidic idol. They privately assume she stole the item but are terrified for her safety; Marrick masks his fear with furious threats while Locke stays calmer but still bristles with potential violence. Off‑screen the druids are holding a formal trial (Sagha or other circle leaders preside) with guardian snakes and charged guards, and the player’s earlier confrontation with Kagha and the Shadow Druid reveal may already have inflamed the grove. Whether Arabella is alive or has been harmed depends on prior events (whether the snake court was stopped); other grove figures (Kagha, Rath, Halsin, Olodan) and any companions present will shape how permissive or hostile the druids are toward the parents.
- DEN_GuardedEntrance_ParentsScene.json: Marricko and Locke are trying to force their way past multiple guards to get into the inner grove. Their daughter was taken by the druids and stands accused of thievery. This is a tense scene - the threat of violence close to the surface. Their daughter is NOT present - she is in the inner chambers of the druid grove.
- DEN_GuardedEntrance_AD_Parents.json: Situation 1: Locke and Marrick have learned their daughter is dead - killed by Sagha and her snake. Situation 2: Locke and Marrick have been denied entry into the inner grove. They are standing close to the entrance trying to figure out their next step. Marrick is happy to charge in but Locke is advising caution. Their daughter is inside.
- CAMP_GoblinHuntCelebration_ParentA.json: Parents are on the beach after the scene with the Druid Leader OR if the scene never happened for whatever reason. Locke's wife Marrick has either murdered Kagha, let her live or is sitting in the dark as others celebrate. Locke is  mainly concerned for his wife at this stage and the effects the events of the night have had on her.

context: Locke and Marrick are standing at the entrance to the inner grove and sacred pool, just denied entry while their daughter Arabella is being held in the druids’ court accused of stealing a druidic idol. They privately believe she took it but are terrified for her safety; Marrick hides his fear behind fury and threats of violence, while Locke stays calmer but is still quick to bristle. Off‑screen, druids (Kagha, Sagha or other circle leaders) and guardian snakes preside over a formal trial in the inner chambers, and whether Arabella is unharmed depends on prior events (for example, whether the snake court was interrupted). The parents are desperate and short‑tempered, so any reassurance or news—truthful or not—will be met with tense, suspicious reactions.
